title: The Wandering Homeland: a policy for environmentally displaced persons

context_sources.name: Boano, Zetter and Morris, environmentally displaced people
IOM discussion note MC/INF/288, migration and the environment, 2007

limitations: A watermark breaks the summation signs in the entropy formulas and the radius-time line.
The competition coefficients are never given numerically, so Figures 7 and 8 cannot be reproduced.
The economic model has no printed equation.
Table 3 has a shifted row: one country name is missing and the last row has no weight.

tasks: Count the people displaced by sea level rise
Assign receiving shares by blame and capacity
Show that cultural protection changes the outcome
Price the gain and loss for each host
Revise the policy where the model exposes unfairness

section_map.summary: Named policy, cone forecast, entropy weights, culture competition, split economic verdict.
Definitions, the UNHCR opening, five tasks.
Survival, carrying capacity, time scale, heritage types, menu-cost analogy.
Eight clauses: duty, direct aid, four indicators, non-refoulement, culture classes.
Cone, entropy weights, Lotka-Volterra, economic account.
Five-year update, exemption, a fund, multilateral heritage work, religion.
Displacement literature, altimetry, World Bank, cost of living.

contributions.summary: A cone scaled to the world gives an annual flow rather than one stock.
Entropy weights checked against a stated expectation before use.
A periodic reallocation and an exemption added because the model itself shows lasting losses.

dependency_graph.handoff: The fifty-year headcount is what the country shares have to absorb
Canada's receiving share fixes how many newcomers arrive by 2070
The cone model supplies the world inflow behind Canada's share
Country shares split the yearly inflow across the twenty hosts
The yearly displaced series drives the cost and value account

assumptions.summary: Only sea-level displacement counts. Storms, floods and quakes are out.
Flooded residents cannot move inland, so all of them leave.
A person carries exactly one culture.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Altimetry fit gives 3.44 mm a year.
Forty years of four indicators for fifty countries, processed in MATLAB.

models.summary: Cone geometry with constant rise and compound density growth.
Four-indicator entropy weighting, top twenty receivers.
Two-species cultural competition under two parameter regimes.
Lagged value minus resettlement and living cost.

verification.summary: Weights judged reliable because they match the expected ordering.
Five rise speeds leave the shape of the yearly curve unchanged.

results_trace.summary: 18,230,968 displaced over fifty years from small islands.
Weights 0.259, 0.239, 0.139, 0.363. Canada, Australia, the United States lead.
Three rich countries cross into profit within three years and pass five billion.

writing_logic.summary: A menu-cost analogy carries a whole argument about the price of moving.
An admitted omission is turned into a lower bound on severity.
The model's own unfair result is what forces the policy revision.

language_observations.summary: Menu costs used to explain why migrants pay to settle.
A computed weight defended by matching an expectation.
A restriction conceded and then used as evidence.
A policy amended in the same paragraph that exposes its flaw.

visualization_observations.summary: Figure 1: mind map of the issue analysis.
Figure 2: city heights above sea level, from several cited sources.
Figure 3: sea level series and its straight-line fit.
Figure 4: the cone standing in for the islands.
Figure 5: the waterline rising on the cone.
Figures 7 and 8: cultural shares with and without protection.
Figures 9 to 13: benefit curves for all hosts and for four subgroups.
Figure 14: the yearly curve under five rise speeds.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Treating an omission as a lower bound makes the severity claim harder to dismiss.
Letting the model's bad result change the policy shows the model does work.
Naming the three bodies of law that fail gives the proposed framework a target.

weaknesses.summary: Competition coefficients are never numbered, so the culture figures cannot be checked.
The economic model is never written as an equation.
Table 3 shifts a row, leaving one country unnamed and the last without a weight.

independent_extensions.summary: Estimate the competition coefficients so Figures 7 and 8 can be reproduced.
Write the economic account as an explicit recurrence and recompute the curves.
Rebuild Table 3 and name the missing country.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Set receiving shares from data-driven weights and check them against a stated expectation.
Recompute obligations on a fixed cycle and exempt states in recognized crisis.

unresolved_questions.question: What numerical competition coefficients produced Figures 7 and 8?
What is the exact yearly account behind the benefit curves?
Which country is missing from the shifted row of Table 3?
